Banana peels. Coffee grounds. That very sad lettuce in the back of the fridge. They’re not the end of the story.

We’re a little club with a big love for the life under our feet.

GOOD DIRT is a fictional neighborhood collective built around a simple idea: when we compost together, food scraps become a resource and the cycle keeps turning. Pull up a bucket and join the fun.

The good stuff

SCRAPS
TO SOIL.

A tiny routine with a full-circle ending. Here’s how a community compost club can work.

COLLECT / AT HOME

Save your scraps.

Keep a little container in your kitchen for fruit and vegetable trimmings, coffee grounds, and more.

CONNECT / LOCALLY

Bring them by.

Find a local compost program and check its drop-off rules. Every pile has its own preferences.

RETURN / TO EARTH

Let nature do its thing.

With time, air, and a little care, those scraps can become rich compost for growing things.

The cheat sheet

CAN I
COMPOST
THIS?

Start with the basics. Rules can vary by collection program, so check with your local compost provider before dropping anything off.

Fruit & veggie scraps

Peels, cores, stems, and that forgotten carrot are usually welcome. Remove produce stickers first.

Coffee & tea

Coffee grounds and loose tea are common compost ingredients. Check whether your collector accepts filters and tea bags.

Paper & cardboard

Some programs accept uncoated, food-soiled paper and torn cardboard. Check local guidance first.

Meat, dairy & oils

These often need special processing and may not be accepted in backyard piles. Ask your local program before adding them.

Come grow with us

GOOD THINGS
ARE GROWING.

Composting is better together. Find a real community garden or local collection program near you, and give those scraps somewhere good to go.
